subject: Geopolitics
title: The Arab Spring Blindspot
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Arab Spring Blindspot usable.

hook.text: In 2011 revolutions swept the Arab world. No major intelligence agency predicted them.

buildup.text: Agencies focused on governments and militaries, not on public frustration, unemployment, and social media activism.

discovery.text: Bottom-up revolutions are harder to predict than top-down coups. Populations don't file memos before they revolt.

twist.text: Social media amplified grievances at a speed no agency could track. By the time analysts caught up, regimes had fallen.

climax.text: The Arab Spring showed that intelligence agencies must monitor societies, not just governments, to predict instability.

punchline.text: The next revolution starts in a crowd, not a cabinet.

quiz.question: Why did intelligence agencies fail to predict the Arab Spring?
options: They didn't have agents in the affected countries
They focused on governments, not on public frustration and social media
The revolutions were planned in total secrecy
